notes:
Trial notes: 3-week Hosted API trial. Lightweight, pragmatic feedback.
- Primary apps: in-product chat assistant (help + code examples), semantic doc search + top-k rerank, periodic batch embedding updates.
- Dev quote: 'Hosted API works great functionally; main concerns are cost predictability and peak latency under shopping-cart traffic spikes.'
- Cost sensitivity: high during price discovery; want clear unit economics by QPS and token mix.
- Security: must be able to sign BAAs; SSO via Okta, audit logs required, keys in KMS. Data residency for EU customers is a plus.
- Procurement: finance wants committed monthly cap for Dedicated; prefers predictable monthly billing vs variable tokens.
- Internal stake: Platform team lead (CTO proxy) is pushing for Dedicated if sizing looks reasonable.
- Tone: pragmatic, engineering-heavy, low appetite for vendor lock-in.
technical_summary: Hosted API trial metrics (aggregated): avg QPS observed: 12 sustained (baseline user sessions). Peak QPS observed during promotional spike test: 85 QPS for ~8 minutes. Avg concurrency observed: 42 concurrent requests during peak windows. Token mix (sampled across endpoints): avg total tokens per call = 920 (prompt ~240, completion ~680). Batch embedding pipeline: 3M tokens/day during nightly runs. Latency targets: p95 end-to-end response target = <600ms for short completions, p99 target desirable for SLO planning. POC recommendation: Dedicated capacity to support baseline 25 QPS with headroom to 100 QPS sustained with burst to 150 QPS; initial sizing estimate = 2 x A100-equivalent nodes with autoscale to 4 under sustained spike, plus caching and prefix-KV for hot flows.
poc_findings: Hosted API functionally validated for reranking and chat flows
Observed token-cost sensitivity on high-frequency assistant prompts — caching could reduce token spend ~18-25%
Latency spikes correlate with long completion lengths and concurrency — batching/quantization options discussed
Embedding ingestion is heavy at night; Dedicated allows isolated throughput and predictable IO
